extracted.intended_audience: Recording Academy Voting and Professional Members, media companies, and music industry entrants submitting recordings for GRAMMY consideration
extracted.subtask_short: GRAMMY awards entry and eligibility rules
extracted.subtask_description: Official rules and guidelines governing eligibility, submission, screening, nominating, and voting processes for the 65th GRAMMY Awards, including category-specific screening criteria and technical requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility period
rubrics_metrics.description: Recordings must be released during the GRAMMY Awards eligibility period (for 65th GRAMMYs: Oct. 1, 2021 to Sept. 30, 2022) and available from any date within the eligibility period through at least the current year’s Final Ballot voting deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recordings must be commercially released, nationally distributed and available through the final ballot deadline; specific calendar dates for entry, voting and deadlines are published. Exceptions for certain formats (e.g., opera, immersive audio album, music video/music film) are noted elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: New recordings definition
rubrics_metrics.description: "New recordings" are material recorded within five years of the release date and not previously released.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recordings not newly recorded are only eligible in specified Categories (Best Historical Album, Best Compilation Soundtrack Album, Best Immersive Audio Album if multichannel mix is new, Best Remixed Recording if remix is new, Best Recording Package, Best Special Package if package is new, Best Album Notes if notes are new), and some classical multidisc exceptions apply (100% previously unreleased material, single artist/ensemble, single composer).

rubrics_metrics.name: General distribution requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: "General distribution" requires broad release nationwide via brick-and-mortar stores, third-party online retailers and/or streaming services; imports are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "Streaming services" are defined as paid subscription, full catalog, on-demand services that have existed in the U.S. for at least one full year as of entry deadline. Spoken word albums may use SoundCloud and e-reader links as exceptions. All entries must have an assigned ISRC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited-edition releases ineligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Limited-edition releases do not meet distribution requirements for eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Academy may inquire into shipment numbers and decide in its discretion whether a release's shipment level makes it eligible based on an artist's typical shipment policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital recording technical & metadata requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Original digital files and products sent to the Academy must have quality comparable to at least 16-bit/44.1 kHz (and 44 kHz/16 bit for specified categories) and include label credits in required metadata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requested documentation (list of retailers/streaming services) must be provided if requested to verify crediting or release date; technical quality specifically required for Best Engineered Album, Non-Classical and Classical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized (non-infringing) recordings
rubrics_metrics.description: Recordings must be non-infringing, original works of authorship; appropriate authorization must be obtained for any third-party copyrighted material embodied in a recording.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If allegations arise that a recording is unauthorized, the Academy will consider the allegations and determine eligibility in its sole discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Singles and tracks definitions & cross-year rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A single is a recording released separately; a track is an individual song released as part of an album; they are judged identically where both eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A track or single from a previous year’s album can be eligible in specified Fields if it was not entered as a track/single the previous year and the album did not win a GRAMMY in a performance Category; a track released on an album in the current year is eligible if not entered as a single the previous year. A single/track is eligible in one specialized Genre Field; albums and their tracks may be screened into different fields. If a single is released one year and its music video a different year, both are eligible in their respective years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Album definition (track count & playing time)
rubrics_metrics.description: An album is a collection of audio recordings issued as a unit: at least five tracks and at least 15 minutes total playing time, or any number of tracks if total playing time is at least 30 minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Updated, revised or expanded versions of previously submitted albums are not eligible. For the 65th GRAMMYs, albums must contain greater than 75% playing time of newly recorded, previously unreleased recordings. To be eligible in a specific Genre Field, an album must contain >50% playing time of that genre. A recording may not be in more than one specialized Genre Field; an album may be in one Field while tracks are in another.

rubrics_metrics.name: Featured artist recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: A featured artist must be credited as a featured artist and must make a significant and artistic contribution beyond accompaniment to be recognized as a GRAMMY nominee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Featured artists are eligible in Album Of The Year and in genre album Categories if they perform >50% of playing time, and in performance Categories if credited as a featured artist on the track/single. Numerous-guest-track albums may be considered 'Various Artists' at Academy discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple mixes and remixes rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Only one version/mix of a recording is eligible in the GRAMMY process in any given year; label chooses which mix to enter when multiple versions are released in the same eligibility year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different film/soundtrack versions may be entered in specific Categories (e.g., Best Song Written For Visual Media). Current remixes/alternate mixes of recordings released in a previous awards year are generally eligible only in Best Remixed Recording. The Category excludes covers, re-recordings, remasters, edits, and addition of a featured vocal without substantive change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampled and interpolated material policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Samples and interpolations are elements of previously released recordings incorporated into new recordings; recordings featuring samples/interpolations are eligible only if the performance up for consideration is newly recorded per Academy definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recordings featuring samples are eligible in songwriting Categories, but writers of sampled/interpolated material are not considered nominees or GRAMMY recipients. Definition examples include isolated sections, hooks, riffs, basslines, background vocals, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voices used as 'instruments' exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Vocal performances are never eligible as instrumental performances, regardless of vocal technique or production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Techniques such as scatting, beatboxing, throat singing, or vocally mimicking instruments do not make a vocal performance eligible as an instrumental performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordings released by the Academy/telecast ineligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Recordings released by the Recording Academy or affiliate-produced releases, including GRAMMY telecast performances, are not eligible in the awards process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes recordings of telecast performances and affiliate-produced releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student recordings eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Student recordings are eligible if they meet all other eligibility requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No special exemption — student recordings must satisfy distribution, release, technical and other general rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Playback systems recordings ineligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: If a specialized piece of equipment is required to play a recording (other than common consumer devices), the recording is not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Pianocorder cassettes that only play on a Pianocorder Reproducing System are not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordings made of playback systems (historical) rule
rubrics_metrics.description: New recordings that capture a playback device playing a previously recorded performance (piano rolls, player piano systems, Zenph, Welte-Mignon, etc.) are not eligible in Best Historical Album.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such playback-system recordings are only eligible in Best Engineered Album when the new recording of the playback is considered; a piano roll itself is not eligible as a 'recording'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translations authorship rule
rubrics_metrics.description: For lyrics or album notes translated/adapted into another language, the original writer is always the eligible writer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translators/adapters are not treated as the original eligible writer for songwriting/notes eligibility purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category screening process & artist intent
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries are screened by genre expert committees to determine appropriate Category and Field placement; Screening Committees should consider the artist’s intent (entry category) when deciding placement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a Screening Committee is unsure, artist intent (initial entry) should be the deciding factor. There is also a National Screening Committee and specific Screening Committees for listed genres (Alternative, American Roots, Blues, etc.). Entries in comedy/spoken word are screened by staff and consult experts if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academy rights to disqualify and reclassify entries
rubrics_metrics.description: The Recording Academy reserves rights to disqualify entries for incorrect/incomplete information or missing required product; to place selections into the Category it deems appropriate; to pass on eligibility; and to designate classifications of achievement to be recognized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Academy makes final determinations of persons entitled to awards, may replace track entries with album entries if >50% playing time is represented, withdraw Categories for insufficient entries, disqualify excessive entries, and take measures against outside influence and bloc voting. Participation does not guarantee a nomination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of entering inappropriately or missing materials
rubrics_metrics.description: If an entry is entered inappropriately and not discovered before the First Ballot mailing, it will be disqualified from the process without liability for further action by the Academy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Academy assumes no liability if judging copies for Craft entries fail to reach the Academy by the due date. Ineligible entries processed during an awards year will be disqualified the following year. Entries may be disqualified for violations of Voting and Solicitation Guidelines or For Your Consideration guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may enter and how (access)
rubrics_metrics.description: All Voting and Professional Recording Academy Members and registered media companies that release eligible recordings during the eligibility period may make GRAMMY entries through the Online Entry Process (OEP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Media companies receive Online User IDs in advance; Voting and Professional Members use member site credentials. Entry Access dates (e.g., July 18 - Aug 31 for 65th) are published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration and per-entry fee policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Media companies pay annual registration fees higher than individual membership fees; members receive five courtesy entries each year and pay per-entry fees after the five free entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee schedule varies by early/standard/final deadlines (examples: Members $40/$75/$125 after 5 courtesy entries; Media Companies $65/$95/$125). Members burdened by fees may request waivers via the Awards Department.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry limits (per-recording limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OEP limits entries in genre Categories to one per recording for albums; limits track/single entries to one for performance Categories and one for song/composition Categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: System-enforced limits help prevent multiple redundant entries; special rules apply for General and Craft Fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of nominations and category size thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: General Field Categories (Record, Song, Album Of The Year, Best New Artist) have 10 nominations; other Categories have five. Ties may expand nominations to up to six or reduce to no less than three.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each Category should have at least 40 distinct artist entries. If a Category receives 25–39 entries, only three nominations will be given; fewer than 25 entries result in the Category going on hiatus for the year (entries screened into another Category). If fewer than 25 entries for three consecutive years, Category discontinued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry list typography allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Entrants may use special characters and unusual typographical treatments in artist names/titles on ballot entry lists so long as characters are found on a computer keyboard or via standard diacritical markings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies to how names/titles appear in the Academy’s entry lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streaming requirements and required physical/digital copies
rubrics_metrics.description: Academy members and media companies must provide eligible streaming links for each entry except certain Craft Categories; specific Categories require additional product copies for judging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Streaming links recommended to facilitate voting. Missing required streaming links or retail-ready product by deadline may result in disqualification. Required copies examples: Album Notes (1 copy); Immersive Audio Album (3 copies); Recording Package (5 copies); Historical Album (3 copies); Producer Of The Year, Non-Classical (4 copies); Engineered Album, Non-Classical (2 copies). Additional copies required if entering same recording in multiple Craft Categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nominating process and 10/3 voting rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominations are determined by Voting Members via first round ballots or Craft Nominating Committees; voters are encouraged to vote in the four General Field Categories and may vote in up to 10 other Categories within no more than three Fields (the 10/3 rule).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change restricts voting breadth to ensure peer relevance; craft nominations may be decided by committee processes described in Craft Nominating Committee Guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft nominating committee membership and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Craft Committee members must be Voting Members in the membership class corresponding to the Craft and must submit a Documentation Form listing six tracks/albums for which they have nomination-eligible credit; credits must be for recordings released in the previous five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The form remains on file for five years. Committee slates are developed by Chapters and other leadership, with final ratification by the National Board of Trustees. No person may serve more than five consecutive years without a break, with specific exceptions for chairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee service terms & turnover requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members may serve fixed terms with required breaks; at least 25% of each committee must turnover from the previous year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Committee members generally serve five years on and one year off; Committee Chairs serve three years on and two years off; at least 25% turnover each year by the fourth year. Some committees (Classical) may add specialists (engineers/producers) as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional/national craft committee voting processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain Craft Categories use Regional or National Craft Nominating Committees that review top selections from the general first-round voting to select final nominations through confidential ballots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For some categories (e.g., Producer Of The Year: top 30; Classical top 50), regional committees of 15 Voting Members or national committees of 25–50 Voting Members meet to judge and select the five nominations. Best Album Notes may be judged remotely through password-protected site and mailed ballots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Songwriter Of The Year, Non-Classical screening criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: This Category recognizes songwriting excellence for non-performing/non-producing songwriters; songwriters must have written a minimum of five songs in which they are credited solely as songwriter or co-writer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Songwriters may supplement core five songs with up to four additional songs where they have other credits (Primary/Featured Artist or Producer), up to a maximum of nine songs. Songs from albums released in a previous year are not eligible; rereleases/remixes/historical recordings not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline and process for claiming nomination corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a two-week deadline after nominations are announced for individuals not credited appropriately to claim nomination status and request corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claimants must inform the Awards Department with details of inaccuracies/omissions, explanations, and corrective steps; Academy may request further documentation. Claims after the deadline are informed that official changes will be made after the awards telecast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenges to GRAMMY Award entitlement procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Challenges to final entitlement decisions by the Awards Department must be made in writing and addressed to the Executive Committee of the Recording Academy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Executive Committee investigates and decides the challenge with powers of the Board of Trustees for that purpose; its decision is final and provided in writing to the challenger.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of nominations any nominee may receive (Rules A–F)
rubrics_metrics.description: A set of rules (A–F) governs how many nominations any nominee may receive, with exceptions for collaborations, co-nominees, music videos/films, and specific rules for Classical entries (e.g., orchestra/co-nominee differences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules include variations such as 1 nomination only (Rule A), no limit (Rule B), 1 nom to artist with exceptions allowing 2 when co-nominees differ, 1 nomination per music video/film, and classical-specific exceptions like 2 nominations for choral conductor if chorus differs. (Full text of Rules A–F should be consulted for case-specific application.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Engineered Album screening criteria (non-classical)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes excellence in engineering for newly recorded non-classical albums; all eligible credited engineers, mixers and mastering engineers on the album are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary judging criterion is the finished product: overall mix, unique techniques, quality of sound, and trueness of reproduction. Overdubbing, number of tracks, site/mode of recordings are secondary considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Producer Of The Year, Non-Classical eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes excellence in production; a producer must have released one album OR six tracks/singles as the minimum to be eligible, up to nine projects may be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If more than nine entries exist, the producer chooses which nine to include. Minimum qualifications may combine solo credits and team credits; the producer must provide at least one eligible single/track producing an artist other than themselves. An individual cannot appear both solo and as part of a producer team on the ballot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Remixed Recording screening criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes excellence in remixed recordings where the remixer creatively adds to, alters or transforms previously recorded/released material to create a new/unique performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category excludes covers, re-recordings, remasters, edits, and mere addition of a featured vocal without substantive change. Singles/tracks need not be commercially released if they were released to clubs/radio in the U.S. for the first time during the eligibility year. Both remixed and original versions must be available to the Academy for judging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Immersive Audio Album technical & eligibility criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes excellence in multichannel immersive audio recordings; eligible recordings must be commercially released on a consumer format/configuration that provides an original immersive mix of four or more channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligible formats include DVD-Video, DVD-Audio, SACD, Blu-ray, Atmos, Auro-3D, immersive download, etc. On releases with multiple distinct mixes, entrant must choose which immersive mix to enter; only one mix per album eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Historical Album screening criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes excellence in newly created albums featuring historically significant material with new annotation and new packaging that contribute to a fresh historical perspective (including quality remastering/audio restoration where relevant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligible entries may include previously released recordings, alternate takes, and unreleased recordings. Straight reissues with no quality restoration or package changes are not eligible. The Category is not for newly recorded re-creations of historic material; up to three compilation producers may be entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contemporary Classical Composition eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes excellence in contemporary classical composition: original compositions composed within the last 25 years, released on a recording for the first time during the eligibility year; eligible compositions must be individual works and world premiere recordings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New operas and classical motion picture/TV compositions are eligible; new versions, arrangements, suites, transcriptions, reorchestrations, remixes, or variants of preexisting compositions are not eligible. Full-length PDF score must be submitted with each entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classical field category-specific definitions (performance/ensemble rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Various Classical Categories set performance/ensemble size and extraction rules: e.g., Orchestral Performance predominantly orchestral by ensembles of 25+; Choral Performance for ensembles of 16+; Chamber Music/Small Ensemble performance for groups not exceeding 24 participants (excluding conductor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choral performances extracted from opera/symphonic recordings are not eligible in Choral Category; orchestral organization is not a nominee (only statuette winner). In categories where both albums and tracks are eligible, if the entire album qualifies then tracks from that album are not eligible in the same Category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Music Video and Music Film screening criteria & materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Best Music Video recognizes excellence in music videos that are synchronous/predominantly synchronous to a commercially released recording and recognized as the official video; Best Music Film recognizes concert/performance films or music documentaries with >50% performance-based material released for the first time in the eligibility year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants must provide active streaming links (YouTube/Vimeo) for music videos and specific digital master file formats or streaming links for music films. Fan videos, re-edits not recognized by the artist/label, episodes of TV/online series, re-edited old programs, compilations of past eligible clips, and biopics are not eligible. A GRAMMY nomination in a performance Category does not affect music video/film eligibility in other years.
